Checks toolchain and inventories all #includes and common libc functions used across torture+c-testsuite, deriving scope/priority from evidence (led to writing stub headers at 168-183).
Verifies SysV ABI empirically: ArgClass enum, small/large struct return tests with asm inspection, 8-int-arg test — confirming argument registers and struct classification against reality.
Drills into stack/member alignment corners (stkalign, align_to, _Alignof with member align), testing and correcting alignment behavior.
Isolates precise semantic corners — integer promotion in xor/cast, bitfield promotion, postfix dec on bitfields — with minimal repros fed back into codegen/parser.
Sustained investigation of SIMD vector semantics/ABI late in the run: repeated minimal repros, asm inspection, and ABI classification fixes — suites treated as an evolving spec.

reasoning: The agent opens with systematic corpus characterization (test runner internals, per-suite and per-chapter feature distribution, include/libc inventory) matching anchor 8, and verifies ABI details (arg registers, struct return classification, alignment) empirically rather than by assumption. It then sustains deep, repro-driven investigation of specific C corners (promotion, bitfields, union init, complex, SIMD, preprocessing) throughout the ~890-step horizon, feeding reference behavior back into design — the hallmark of anchor 10. I place it at 9 rather than a clean 10 because the log exposes only tool-call titles, so I cannot fully confirm the depth of the mental models behind each drill-down.
